elements.evidence: The added operative language states that “Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to Vendor.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly requires “thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to Vendor.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees following Customer’s termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: Vendor must refund prepaid Fees attributable to the period after the effective termination date, which implements a pro-rata refund of unused prepaid fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that “Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a term.”
The added operative language grants Customer a termination-for-convenience right for the Agreement or any Order Form.

elements.element: Customer’s termination-for-convenience right requires between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days’ notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only thirty (30) days’ prior written notice, not notice within the specified 60–90 day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that no early-termination fee or other penalty applies, so the conditional cap is satisfied because no such fee is payable.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause denies Vendor a termination-for-convenience right during a term but does not affirmatively grant or define a right exercisable at the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor’s termination for convenience requires ninety (90) days’ notice.
elements.evidence: No operative language grants Vendor a termination-for-convenience right subject to ninety days’ notice.

result.reason: The operative redline fully satisfies the preferred position: Customer receives a 30-day written-notice termination right, an unused-prepaid-fee refund, and Vendor is barred from convenience termination during a term. It does not satisfy the fallback’s different notice structure or Vendor termination mechanism. The change is not strictly minimal because “in whole or in part” adds a partial-termination right beyond what is required by the preferred position. The drafting otherwise preserves the existing termination provisions, but quality is reduced because the new paragraph is unnumbered and uses the potentially ambiguous lowercase term “a term.”
